source: Roadmap §4 (beta.5: a service caller first declared api-key, a method of its own before RC1); coordinator's decision of 2026-11-23 (design (b): AuthenticatedPrincipal.workload); RFC 0009 §3, §4.2, RFC 0010 C3 (sentences proposed in the PR)
statement: The identity a service states for itself when it calls the control plane as its own principal (ControlCaller.service, ServiceIdentity), in process or over the network, names its credential `service`, never `api-key` or `jwt`, with the id `service:<principal>`, and audit and decision records name the method so. A change record's origin names how the call came (CTL-57): `via.method: service` over the network, and `via.method: in-process` through the in-process facade (CTL-65), each with the credential id `service:<principal>`. `service` and `api-key` are workloads' credentials by construction (IDN-44): a credential so named cannot be declared a person's, whoever made it, a gateway's forwarded identity, a service's stated one or another authenticator. A principal is a workload's (AuthenticatedPrincipal.workload) when its credential declares itself a workload's, when it has none, or when CoSec's API key authenticator proved it (by provenance). What a principal may do as a person or as a workload is read from workload alone, never from apiKey, which keeps its meaning (an API key proved it): a workload never approves (APR-7) and is never the trust root (APR-3). A `service` credential, as any credential but CoSec's own token, has no session and no break-glass. A principal another authenticator proves is what its credential declares (Identity.Credential.kind, a required parameter, IDN-44): the method it names is a label and decides nothing (an S3 of the RC1 review, DR1-C-3, closed by IDN-44).
guards: spi:AuthenticatedPrincipalTest#a workload is what its credential declares, an API key by provenance, or a principal with no credential - IDN-44
spi:AuthenticatedPrincipalTest#a service's credential has no break-glass and no session - IDN-34
runtime:ServiceIdentityTest#a service's identity names its credential service - IDN-34
runtime:ServiceIdentityTest#admitted, a service's identity is a workload's, without break-glass - IDN-34
runtime:IdentityGateTest#a forwarded service identity is a workload's credential, without break-glass - IDN-34
control:ApprovalB2Test#a service's own identity never approves - IDN-34
control:ApprovalB2Test#a service's own identity is never the trust root - IDN-34
architecture:WorkloadCredentialTest#whether a principal is a workload is read from workload, never from apiKey alone - IDN-34
